nonop.text: Our results of operations depend generally on net interest income, which is the difference between interest income from interest-earning assets and interest expense on interest-bearing liabilities. Net interest income is affected by regulatory, economic and competitive factors that influence interest rates, loan demand and deposit flows. In addition, we are subject to interest rate risk to the degree that our interest-earning assets mature or reprice at different times, or at different speeds, than our interest-bearing liabilities. Our results of operations are also affected by noninterest income, such as service charges, wealth management fees, loan fees, gains from the sale of newly originated loans, gains or losses on investments and certain other noninterest related items. Our principal operating expenses, aside from interest expense, consist of compensation and employee benefits, occupancy costs, professional fees, data processing expenses and provision for credit losses.

pretax.text: Our income before taxes was $38.7 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $13.1 million in the third quarter of 2025. Net interest and dividend income increased $1.3 million, and provision for credit losses decreased $12.9 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to the like 2025 quarter. Noninterest income decreased nominally while noninterest expense declined $11.5 million. The noninterest expense decrease of $11.5 million is primarily due to an $8.9 million decrease in salary and employee benefits expense primarily attributable to Bancorp Financial acquisition related costs for change in control, retention and severance payments. Also contributing to the decrease in noninterest expense was a $744,000 decrease in computer and data processing, a $1.7 million decrease in professional fees, and a $343,000 decrease in other expenses, which were all primarily driven by the Bancorp Financial acquisition costs that were recorded in the third quarter of 2025. Our net income was $28.9 million, or $0.56 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026, compared to net income of $9.9 million, or $0.18 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025. We continue to monitor macroeconomic conditions, interest rate risk, expense levels, and daily liquidity.

tax.text: Net income for the third quarter of 2026 was $28.9 million, or $0.56 per diluted share, compared to $28.2 million, or $0.54 per diluted share, for the second quarter of 2026, and $9.9 million, or $0.18 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025. Net income increased compared to the prior year like quarter, primarily due to the absence of acquisition related expense, and the Day Two non-PCD provision recorded in connection with the Bancorp Financial acquisition in the 2025 period. Variances in the year over year period included a decrease of $3.3 million in interest expense, a decrease of $12.9 million in provision for credit losses, and a decrease of $11.5 million in noninterest expense, partially offset by a $2.0 million decrease in interest and dividend income and a $6.6 million increase in provision for income taxes. Net income in the third quarter of 2026 was negatively impacted by provision for credit losses of $6.8 million, compared to $7.5 million and $19.7 million recorded in the second quarter of 2026 and third quarter of 2025, respectively. The $19.7 million recorded in the third quarter of 2025 was due to purchase accounting adjustments and the Day Two non-PCD provision for loan losses recorded of $13.2 million.

ocf.text: Liquidity is our ability to fund operations, to meet depositor withdrawals, to provide for customers’ credit needs, and to meet maturing obligations and existing commitments. Our liquidity principally depends on our cash flows from operating activities, investment in and maturity of assets, changes in balances of deposits and borrowings, and our ability to borrow funds. Through the third quarter of 2026, we experienced a decrease in loans and deposits. We managed the change in our funding through an increase in average borrowings from the FHLBC through September 30, 2026, compared to the prior year end. We seek to ensure our funding needs are met by maintaining a level of liquidity through asset and liability management. We monitor our borrowing capacity at the FHLBC as part of our liquidity management process as supervised by our Asset and Liability Committee (“ALCO”) and reviewed by our Board of Directors. In addition, our senior management team monitors cash balances daily to ensure we have adequate liquidity to meet our operational and financing needs. As of September 30, 2026, our cash on hand liquidity totaled $108.1 million, a decrease of $15.9 million from cash balances held as of December 31, 2025.
